# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 8
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 8

---

*[The Eucharistic prayer and the prayer over oil. Mygdonia seeks Thomas. A liturgical chapter.]*

1. After baptizing the believers, Thomas broke bread, gave thanks over it, and prayed: "Come, O holy name of Christ that is above every name; come, power of the Most High and perfect mercy; come, thou highest gift; come, compassionate mother; come, thou that knowest the mysteries of the Chosen One; come, thou who art present in all the movements of the Chosen One; come, Holy Spirit, and purify their hearts and seal them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit."

2. Having offered this prayer, he broke the eucharist and gave a portion to each, saying: "Let this eucharist be for you life and forgiveness of sins and eternal resurrection."

3. They answered: "Amen."

4. Present there was a woman named Mygdonia, wife of Charisius, a kinsman of the king. She saw Thomas and was greatly drawn to him.

5. She pressed through the crowd and stood at his side.

6. Thomas saw her and said: "Who are you, and what do you seek?"

7. She said: "I am Mygdonia. I wish to hear from you the word of life."

8. Thomas said: "Blessed are you, Mygdonia, for you have sought what is truly needful. I will give you the living water that quenches all thirst and the bread of heaven that satisfies all hunger."

9. He gave her the eucharist, and she received it with joy.

10. When night came, Thomas took oil and poured it over his own head and prayed: "Come, holy name of Christ; come, power of the Most High; come, gift of the Most High; come, compassionate father; come, fellowship of the male; come, revealer of hidden mysteries; come, mother of the seven houses, whose rest was in the eighth house; come, elder of the five members — intelligence, thought, prudence, reflection, reasoning — communicate with these young men."

11. After anointing with oil, he prayed over those present: "Let the mercy of the Holy Spirit come and rest upon them."

---
*LOGOS note: The Holy Spirit is invoked in both feminine and masculine terms across vv.1 and 10 — "compassionate mother" and "compassionate father." This reflects the Syriac fluidity in Spirit-language. The "seven houses" / "eighth house" may refer to the seven heavens and the ogdoad of Gnostic cosmology, or the seven days of creation and the eschatological sabbath-rest.*
